_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Hagar wept in the wilderness, her water gone.
And God heard the voice of the boy.
He opened her eyes, and there was a well.
The God who sees does not forget us.
Do not be afraid, says Jesus; even the sparrow is counted.
We are worth more than many sparrows.
Come, let us worship the God who hears.
We come, unafraid. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture the wilderness at noon — the skin of water empty, the throat dry, no shade and no road home.
The God who sees is here.
Hagar set the child under a bush and turned away, unable to watch him die — and God heard, and opened her eyes to a well.
The God who sees is here.
Jesus says the hairs of your head are numbered, and not one sparrow falls without your Father knowing.
The God who sees is here.
So whatever desert you crossed to get to this room, you were never out of God's sight for a moment.
The God who sees is here. Do not be afraid!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Hagar's water was gone, the wilderness wide.
The God who sees is here.
God heard the boy and opened her eyes to a well.
The God who sees is here.
Not one sparrow falls outside the Father's knowing.
The God who sees is here.
Come, let us worship, and put down our fear.
The God who sees is here. Amen.
